channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Nvidia Bull Says Huang’s Return Restores Tech Leadership
item.description: StoneX senior semiconductor research analyst Cody Acree upgraded Nvidia to Buy with a $270 price target following Jensen Huang’s return as CEO, saying his reinstatement removes key uncertainties around Nvidia’s technology roadmap, industry relationships and support for the AI buildout. Acree discusses why he sees Huang’s leadership as critical to the investment case with Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Nvidia's Huang to Face Bipartisan Scrutiny on Capitol Hill
item.description: Newly reinstated Nvidia Corp. chief executive officer Jensen Huang will testify publicly before a powerful Senate committee on Dec. 3, according to a statement from the panel’s chairman. Bloomberg's Nathan Dean joins to discuss how Trump's push to reinstate Huang could effect the upcoming hearings. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Anthropic Dips Below IPO Price in Sharp Tech Reversal
item.description: Anthropic PBC shares sank 8% below their $83 initial public offering price, wiping out gains for investors who piled into the artificial intelligence lab’s record-setting debut last week. Bloomberg's Carmen Reinicke joins to discuss. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Nvidia Board Faces Growing Scrutiny, Trade Fears Return
item.description: Get a jump start on the US trading day with Dani Burger on "Bloomberg Open Interest." Stocks slide as the Nvidia euphoria fades and trade fears return. Nvidia is still at the center of the storm. Cleo Capital’s Sarah Kunst says board members should resign, Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi raises national security concerns, and Harvard’s Jesse Fried weighs the board’s duty to shareholders. Plus, Matt Maley on cracks in the AI trade, Anthropic falls below its IPO price, and retailers deliver a bright spot. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: HPE Customers Did Not Change Behavior Due to Nvidia, CEO Neri Says
item.description: Hewlett Packard Enterprise gave a revenue forecast that fell short of estimates, but Chief Executive Officer Antonio Neri is still bullish and says free cash flow for shareholders will keep growing. Neri also says customers did not change their behavior due to the Nvidia drama involving CEO Jensen Huang. Neri speaks on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Jensen Huang Apologizes to Nvidia Staff in All-Hands Meeting
item.description: Nvidia Corp. Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang apologized to employees for the conduct that led to his brief ouster, telling staff at an all-hands meeting on Tuesday that he had let them down, according to people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Ian King, Ed Ludlow and Riley Griffin

item.title: San Francisco Faces Onslaught of Tidal Floods Juiced by El Niño
item.description: San Francisco’s waterfront is facing a stretch of near-record “king tides” this week, threatening flooding just as Thanksgiving travel picks up across the region.
item.dc:creator: Lauren Rosenthal

item.title: Nvidia Is a ‘Good Corporate Citizen,’ Attorney General Says
item.description: US Attorney General Todd Blanche said Nvidia Corp. is “a good corporate citizen,” while declining to directly answer questions about whether the Justice Department is scrutinizing the circumstances that led to the temporary exit of Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang.
item.dc:creator: Georgia Fearn and Chris Strohm

item.title: Airtel Money Is Indicated to Join Ranks of Britain’s Blue Chips
item.description: Less than two months on from its London market debut, Airtel Money is poised to break into the UK’s blue-chip stocks index.
item.dc:creator: Paul Jarvis

item.title: XAI Founders Unveil New AI Startup to Predict Future Events
item.description: Three founding members of Elon Musk’s artificial intelligence business, xAI, have teamed up to build a new AI company with the ambitious goal of predicting future events.
item.dc:creator: Natasha Mascarenhas and Carmen Arroyo

item.title: Congressman Questions Huang Reinstatement
item.description: Democratic Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi is raising national security concerns over Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s reinstatement, citing unanswered questions about alleged access to sensitive information. He also criticized US chip export controls and called for Congress to strengthen oversight of advanced semiconductor exports to China. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Nvidia's Board Members Should Resign, Cleo Capital's Kunst Says
item.description: Sarah Kunst, the founder and managing director of Cleo Capital joins Bloomberg Open Interest to weigh in on Nvidia’s boardroom turmoil and Jensen Huang’s return as CEO. She argues the reversal raises serious questions about corporate governance and integrity. She says Nvidia board members should resign after voting to bring back Huang. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Why AI Pilots Struggle to Scale
item.description: AI is moving from pilots into production, but many companies still need modern infrastructure and teams ready to work differently according to Kyndryl CEO Martin Schroeter. He joins Bloomberg Open Interest to discuss scaling AI, how to protect sovereignty and manage the risks of upgrading complex systems. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Anthropic Shares Fall Below IPO Price of $83
item.description: Anthropic PBC shares sank 6% below their $83 initial public offering price, wiping out gains for investors who piled into the artificial intelligence lab’s record-setting debut last week. Bloomberg's Carmen Reinicke reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: How Dual-Class Stock Entrenches Founder Control at Anthropic, SpaceX, Google
item.description: The AI boom is eroding the principle of "one share, one vote" that checks the power of company founders.
item.dc:creator: Lu Wang

item.title: Anthropic-Backed Startup Led by Ex-Hg Executives Pushes Europe to Build AI Edge
item.description: An Anthropic PBC-backed artificial intelligence consultancy started earlier this month by three former executives of private equity firm Hg is looking to hire “Europe’s elite AI talent” as it seeks to push the continent to catch up on the technology.
item.dc:creator: James Booth

item.title: Nvidia Remains at the Core of AI Growth, Says Ivan Feinseth
item.description: A selloff in technology giants dragged down stocks, with the market also retreating on concerns over fresh US tariffs. Skepticism surfaced over whether the artificial-intelligence trade can mount a sustained rebound, with the Nasdaq 100 falling 1.5%. Nvidia Corp. lost 5%. Anthropic PBC sank below its $83 initial public offering price. Ivan Feinseth, CIO and Senior Partner at Tigress Financial Partners, explains why he remains bullish on tech and why he's maintaining his strong buy rating on Nvidia. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Retailers Post Strong Earnings Ahead of Holidays
item.description: Dick’s Sporting Goods raised its forecast as its Foot Locker chain returned to growth amid robust back-to-school shopping. Best Buy also raised sales and earnings forecasts for the year after reporting better-than-expected quarterly earnings on resilient demand for computing. Emily Cohn reports on "Bloomberg Open Interest." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Amazon Launches Satellites for Network to Rival Starlink
item.description: A European rocket blasted off Tuesday carrying 36 satellites for Amazon.com Inc.’s orbital communications network that the technology giant hopes will rival Elon Musk’s Starlink.
item.dc:creator: Summer Maxwell

item.title: HPE Forecast Trails Top Estimates, Shares Fall on AI Growth Outlook
item.description: Hewlett Packard Enterprise Co. shares dropped the most in more than six years after investors feared that continuing component costs will cut into the hardware company’s profitability next year despite rising revenue.
item.dc:creator: Dina Bass
